* Lay out unformatted (format: false) output readably

With format: false the generator's raw text was flush-left, unpunctuated,
wrapped every union and intersection in parentheses and printed const
objects as JSON. The generator now indents members by depth, terminates
interface members with semicolons, parenthesizes only where precedence
requires (array element, spread, a set operation nested in another),
breaks unions that do not fit on a line (or have commented members) one
member per line, wraps long intersections after each `&`, prints
const/enum object values as type literals and aligns the default banner.

Prettier normalizes all of these, so format: true output is unchanged:
the e2e suite, 46 real-world schemas and 5 600 generated schemas format
to byte-identical text before and after. Top-level type aliases keep no
trailing semicolon on purpose: one in prettier's input makes prettier 3
rebuild the whole source once per comment.

generateType is memoized per node, so each construct renders from
column 0 and its embedder re-indents nested lines; whether a render is a
bare `A | B` / `A & B` is recorded when the text is made, since the
optimizer may rewrite params after children were rendered.

* README: recommend --no-format for very large schemas, with measured figures

The `format` option row and the "giant file" FAQ now say what turning
Prettier off buys (azure / FHIR / k8s: two to three times faster, about
half the memory, from bench/bench.mjs) and that the output stays readable;
the option's doc comment and --help text say the same in one line.

* Keep tsType text, one-branch combinators and verbatim comments byte-identical when formatted

A differential check of formatted (format: true) output against master found inputs the
new layout moved:

- a union whose first member is a one-branch oneOf/anyOf/allOf around a described object
  put the comment after the `|` instead of before it;
- a function or constructor tsType first in a union that no longer fit on one line ended
  up behind a leading `|`, which does not parse;
- a tuple's tsType rest element lost the parentheses it needs when the text is, say,
  `keyof A`;
- a tsType ending in `;` got a second one;
- a comment prettier prints verbatim (one with a lone carriage return in it) lost the
  space after `*` on blank lines and gained a blank line per CRLF;
- a multi-line tsType (a template literal type, say) had its continuation lines indented,
  which inside a template literal changes the type.

tsType text is now taken at its word: a union or intersection with a member whose text is
not a plain type reference is written the one way it always has been (one line, in
parentheses); a rest element keeps its parentheses unless it plainly needs none; and a
multi-line tsType keeps its lines at their columns (its line breaks carried as `\r` while
the declaration is laid out and written back as `\n` on its way out, the mechanism
verbatim comments already used). A one-branch combinator renders as its branch, comment
and all. The layout fixture gains a case for each.

* Put a widened index signature's member comments where a union's go

A one-member allOf/anyOf/oneOf whose member is a described object renders as
that object below its comment. As a member of a widened index signature the
comment now goes before the member's `|`, as it does in any other union (and
as the formatter has always printed it), instead of after it.

* Keep a described lone branch's comment before the `|` when its array leads a union

An array whose element is a one-member `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` around a described
anonymous object renders as that object below its comment, then `[]`. As the first
member of a union (a property's `anyOf`, a widened index signature) the comment now
goes where any member's does, before the `|`, so the formatted output matches what
it has always been; unformatted, `readonly` before such a type loses its trailing space.

* Render a lone branch before asking whether it rendered as a bare union

The one-member path of generateSetOperation read `bareSetOperations` before the
member's text was made, so an array of a lone `oneOf` around a tuple type with
optional elements lost the parentheses around its `[] | [A] | [A, B]` union.

* Render a union member before asking whether it rendered below a comment

memberOf read `commentedTypes` before the member's text was made, so the first
render of an array of a described lone branch — anything under a tuple, which the
optimizer does not visit first — still put the comment after the `|`. Same reorder
as the one-member path; fixtures for the tuple and tuple-rest cases.

* Pin the unformatted layout of described `const` and inline `enum` union members

A layout fixture for the members master now keeps descriptions on: a described
`const`, a described inline `enum`, and arrays of each (string literal, number
literal, union of literals), plus the `readonly` variants through the
type-style twin.

* Put a described member's comment right above it when the member brings its own lines

A described inline `enum` too long for one line is written a member per line,
starting on a new line; placing the comment above it left an empty line in
between, which the formatter keeps. The comment now sits directly above the
member's first line. Adds a layout fixture for the case.

* Keep a described member's comment before the `|` when `| undefined` is appended to it

With `undefinedOptionalProperties`, an optional property whose type rendered as
a type below a comment (an `allOf` of one described inline `enum`, say) had
`| undefined` appended to the parenthesized whole, which put the comment
inside the first member; master's text has it above the union. The comment
now goes where the union's member comments go. `commentedOperand` is the
shared "type below a comment, as one operand" lookup for this and the array
case. Adds a layout fixture (the type-style twin covers `| undefined`).

---------
